h1: Sheet metal fiber laser cutting machines — 5 × 10 ft to 13 × 82 ft, 3 to 40 kW
intro: A fiber laser cutting machine cuts sheet and plate from a DXF file with a focused beam — mild steel to 1-1/2″, stainless and aluminum to 1″ and more with the high-power sources — at speeds no plasma or punch can match, with a clean edge and no tooling. NovoTech sells Dener fiber lasers in Canada: the GFL production laser with a 1.5 G gantry and pallet changer in 5 × 10, 6.6 × 13 and 6.6 × 20 ft, and the Smart series — closed-type with double table in six sizes to 41 ft, semi-closed single table to 13 × 82 ft, and the open-type entry machine — all with IPG, Raycus or nLIGHT sources from 3 to 40 kW, Precitec autofocus heads and nesting software. Loading towers, sheet storage and bevel heads are available. Installed and supported from Mississauga, ON.

faq.q: What laser power do I need?
faq.a: Power sets the thickness and the speed. As a guide for mild steel: 3 kW cuts 1/2″, 6 kW 3/4″ (and 1/4″ at over 300 in/min), 12 kW 1″, 20 kW 1-1/4″ and 30 – 40 kW 1-1/2″ and beyond; stainless and aluminum run about 20 – 30 % thinner at the same power, with nitrogen or air assist. Most Canadian job shops buying today choose 6 or 12 kW: thick enough for structural work, fast enough to pay for the machine on thin sheet. Tell us your material mix and we run the cutting chart for you.

faq.q: GFL or Smart — what is the difference?
faq.a: Both come from Dener's Kayseri plant with the same sources, heads and software. The GFL is the production machine: a heavier stress-relieved frame and space-frame bridge rated for 1.5 G, a pallet changer and the full option list — the machine for two shifts a day. The Smart series is built to a lower price: the closed-type still has a double exchange table and 1 G, the semi-closed machines offer very large single tables, and the open-type is the entry-level 3 – 6 kW laser. Same cut quality; the GFL is faster between parts and lasts longer at high duty.

The model number is the nominal working area in centimetres: 3015 = 10 × 5 ft (3,000 × 1,500 mm) — a standard 4 × 8 or 5 × 10 sheet; 4020 = 13 × 6.6 ft; 6020 = 20 × 6.6 ft for 6 × 20 plate; 6025 and 8025 = 20 and 26 ft × 8.2 ft; 12526 = 41 × 8.5 ft. The 5 × 10 machine is the Canadian standard; buy the 6020 if you cut 20 ft plate or want to nest several sheets without reloading.

faq.q: What about assist gas and fume extraction?
faq.a: Oxygen gives the fastest cut and an oxide edge on mild steel; nitrogen a clean, paint-ready edge on all metals; compressed air at 16 bar replaces nitrogen on sheet to about 1/4″ and cuts the gas bill to near zero — the intelligent air-cutting package is an option. The machines have pneumatic extraction compartments under the table and connect to a dust collector, which we can supply.

Yes — a loading / unloading tower that feeds the pallet changer, sheet storage with several shelves for lights-out production, part sorting, and bevel heads for weld preparation. The GFL and the closed-type Smart are prepared for the tower; ask us for the automation layout.

faq.q: What does the machine need on site?
faq.a: A level floor, 600 V 3-phase (with the transformer we supply) or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas, a dust collector and a compressed-air supply for air cutting. A 6 kW 3015 draws about 30 kW in total. Delivery, installation and operator training are done by NovoTech from Mississauga.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
